title: Radio waves
kid: The access point turns each parcel into ones and zeros and sends them through the air on an invisible radio wave. Big wiggles mean 1, small wiggles mean 0!
nerd: Bits modulate a 2.4/5/6 GHz carrier. Shown here as simple amplitude-shift keying; real Wi-Fi uses OFDM with up to 4096-QAM, packing 12 bits into every symbol on hundreds of sub-carriers.
extra: Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be): with multi-link operation (MLO) the phone and the access point use 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz at the same time, as one link. Channels in the 6 GHz band can be 320 MHz wide, twice Wi-Fi 6E's widest, and with 4096-QAM that makes up to about 46 Gbit/s in theory.

describe.kid: A phone and a Wi‑Fi access point face each other. A wiggly radio wave runs between them. Coloured 1 and 0 bits ride above it, and lines point each bit to a tall or small wiggle. Rings spread from the Wi‑Fi box as the signal moves through the air.
describe.nerd: The scene shows the phone and access point joined by an animated carrier wave. Bits scroll along the track. Stems connect each bit to the wave’s amplitude, as a simplified ASK modulation view. Expanding rings at the access point show the radio signal spreading.
